key_insight: PostTrainBench introduces a focused benchmark showing that LLM agents can autonomously perform many post-training tasks within bounded compute (e.g., a 10-hour budget), exposing which steps are reliably automatable and where human oversight remains necessary.
problem_solved: Evaluates whether and how LLM-based agents can automate the post-training phase that converts base models into usable assistants, under realistic time and compute constraints.
method: Design PostTrainBench: a modular task suite that represents typical post-training steps (data preparation, tuning/optimization, evaluation, deployment checks) with fixed compute/time budgets.
Run agentic LLMs that plan, use tools, and schedule operations to attempt end-to-end post-training workflows within the 10-hour constraint, logging outcomes, resource use, and decisions.
Analyze performance, failure modes, and task-level automability to identify where agents succeed, fail, or require human intervention.
impact: Gives researchers and practitioners a standardized way to measure and develop agentic tooling for finishing models, helping teams decide which post-training steps can be safely delegated to agents and how to allocate human oversight and compute budgets.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart showing post-training steps (data → tuning → evaluation → deployment) with icons for agent/human handoffs
Bar chart or tradeoff plot of task success rate vs. compute/time consumption (e.g., within a 10-hour budget)
Heatmap or matrix indicating automability of each subtask (automatable, partial, human-required)
Example agent timeline (Gantt-style) illustrating planned steps, tool calls, and where failures or interventions occurred
paper_title: PostTrainBench: Can LLM Agents Automate LLM Post-Training?
paper_authors: Ben Rank, Hardik Bhatnagar, Ameya Prabhu, Shira Eisenberg, Karina Nguyen
